scope: Node numeric-buffer-only prototype comparison, not browser capture. All 36 measured pushFrame runs include RGBA input copying, JS sharing/clustering/diagnostics and exact C Float64 dense processing. Production zero-extra-copy conversion requires separate browser evidence.

perFrameStateProof.adjustment: Only explicitly calculated extra allocation in quality.spatial.stateBytes; finiteFloat64/NaNsemanticstate and callbacks match after every push/reset.

memory1080.scope: Temporal state moved into fixed WASM pages; no per-frame state copy. JS clustering, sharing, diagnostics and cache remain outside.

prototypeBoundaries: Node-only top-level file read/synchronous module loading; no browser loader or initial capability fallback implemented.
External RGBA is copied into WASM input and that cost is included; direct native VideoFrame.copyTo into this view remains unproven.
Memory grows only before views exist; same-size resets preserve input/timestamp backing. Runtime buffer identity guard and exact fixed maximum remain production hardening work.
Geometry replacement copies the512KiB timestamp array once to preserve otherwise unused baseline epoch tails; no per-frame temporal state copy.
Allocation figures describe engine state, not process/GPU/code memory or transient GC peaks.
A trap interrupts/resets and throws; it never retries a partially consumed frame through JS.

originalPrototypeProof.scope: Per-push complete temporal arrays including full frameTimes, state metadata, partial findings/diagnostics and callbacks; exact original Float64 finite values and semantic NaN equality. Complete finish reports differ only by explicitly accounted WASM memory allocation. Exact complete finish() and live callback differential; both byte array types, unaligned fallback, alpha and black resets, aliases that fork/reconverge, source geometry changes, timestamp gaps and explicit interruption. Numeric buffers only, never rendered.
